papers.title: Topological Entropy of Group Cellular Automata is Effectively Computable
papers.abstract: Topological entropy is a fundamental invariant of dynamical systems, quantifying their complexity. For cellular automata, however, determining topological entropy is generally algorithmically intractable. We study group cellular automata, namely cellular automata over a finite group alphabet whose global map is a group endomorphism. In dimension one, we decompose topological entropy into two one-sided components describing information propagating from the left and from the right in space--time. We introduce finite families of left and right traces and prove that the entropy is the sum of their growth rates. Hence, the entropy is completely determined by the growth rate of a fixed-width family of space--time patterns. This reduction from arbitrarily large windows to uniformly bounded width yields an effective procedure for computing the entropy. In particular, the entropy of every one-dimensional group cellular automaton is the logarithm of a positive integer. Using Pontryagin duality and the Bridge Theorem between topological and algebraic entropy, we also derive an explicit formula for linear cellular automata over $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^n$ in terms of their characteristic polynomial. Moreover, in every dimension $D\geq 2$, a group cellular automaton is either equicontinuous with zero entropy or sensitive to initial conditions with infinite entropy. Combined with decidability of equicontinuity, this implies that topological entropy is effectively computable from the local rule in every dimension. Thus, group cellular automata form a natural nontrivial class in which algebraic structure restores computability of topological entropy.

papers.title: Visibility graphs of irregularly sampled two-dimensional fields via Voronoi tessellations
papers.abstract: Visibility graphs map a time series into a network by linking two data whenever the straight line between them is not obstructed by intermediate data. Their extension to two-dimensional fields has so far been restricted to regular lattices, where visibility is checked along a finite number of lattice directions. We propose a definition for scalar data sampled at arbitrary, irregularly scattered points of the plane. Each point is assigned its Voronoi cell, so that the data become a landscape of prisms, and two points are linked when the line of sight between them clears the cells crossed by the connecting segment. This yields horizontal ($\HVGV$) and natural ($\NVGV$) Voronoi visibility graphs that reduce exactly to the classical horizontal and natural visibility graphs when the points are collinear, contain the Gabriel graph of the point set, and can be built by an exact walk through the Delaunay triangulation. For uncorrelated heights, the horizontal graph depends only on the ranks of the data, so its statistics are independent of the marginal distribution. The probability that two points see each other is $2/[(M+1)(M+2)]$, where $M$ is the number of Voronoi cells crossed, which reduces the problem to the geometry of the tessellation. For Poisson points this gives a degree distribution with a scale-free tail $P(k)\simeq(\pi^3/4)\,k^{-2}$ and a mean degree that grows as $(\pi^3/8)\ln N$, in contrast with the finite value $\langle k\rangle=4$ of one-dimensional series. Two dimensions are therefore the marginal case in which isotropic horizontal visibility ceases to be local. Numerical simulations with up to $N=1.28\times10^5$ points support these predictions.

papers.title: Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition: Information, Uncertainty, and Conditional Regime Inference
papers.abstract: When do mode energies preserve regime information as measurement quality changes? Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition (sKMD) fits joint regime laws on signed KMD mode coordinates and transfers the reference mode posterior to regime probabilities and conditional reconstructions. For centered Gaussian regimes with independently varying known noise variances, fixed coordinate energies retain the full regime posterior precisely when all classes share their cross-covariances and class variances can differ only at isolated vertices of the covariance graph. We extend the characterization to nonzero means and show that freely varying correlated noise forces a fixed linear log-odds decoder to retain the full quadratic feature span even for two distinct centered regimes. At fixed quality, a three-regime example has no sufficient two-energy basis. Its smallest Bayes log-loss gap over bases of condition number at most $\kappa$ has sharp order $\kappa^{-1}$. Exact Bayes energy posteriors supply numerical gap estimates for specified bases. Additional bounds relate feature compression, independently learned mode spans and sensor-noise error to log loss. Two controlled experiments with 64 independent panels each show that signed information can improve prediction over energy summaries, while integration gives small gains over strong signed controls and depends on how the competing point rule is calibrated and how accurately observation noise is measured.

papers.title: On the statistical reliability of chaotic simulations at reduced precision
papers.abstract: Reduced-precision arithmetic is increasingly used to accelerate scientific simulation, while AI workloads are driving its growing prominence in hardware design. Yet small arithmetic errors do not necessarily imply accurate statistics. Finite representation limits spatial resolution, while rounding can merge trajectories that should separate in chaotic systems, progressively concentrating probability on a shrinking collection of computer states. This redistribution can distort statistical averages well before periodicity becomes apparent; furthermore, disjoint computational basins can induce an initialisation bias, even when the intended equilibrium statistics are independent of the initial ensemble. We use functional graphs and their transfer operators to connect these pathologies to bounds on statistical bias, the duration of accurate averaging, and the effect of reducing precision. Exhaustive numerical experiments on four chaotic maps, with 1-24 significand bits and the 24-bit endpoint matching IEEE FP32, show how initially accurate ensembles drift towards incorrect statistics, with lower precision often bringing this deterioration forward. Stochastic rounding substantially extends some useful averaging windows but leaves others severely biased. Longer computed trajectories can therefore worsen inferred statistics, and a finite average can outperform the "infinite-time" computer average by orders of magnitude. This exposes a risk of statistically biased inference at reduced precision and provides a further motivation for collecting statistics from ensembles of shorter trajectories.

papers.title: The role of distributed friction dynamics on heave-induced motion of offshore drilling systems: modelling, analysis, and simulations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the influence of friction dynamics on heave-induced disturbance propagation using a coupled hydraulic-structural drilling model formulated as a semilinear interconnection of ordinary and hyperbolic partial differential equations (ODE-PDEs), and capturing spatially distributed memory effects in the drillstring-wellbore interaction. First, local and global existence and uniqueness results are established, and sufficient conditions for boundedness and input-to-state stability are deduced via a small-gain analysis. Subsequently, extensive numerical investigations are carried out, including harmonic excitation studies, nonlinear distortion analysis, spatial amplification investigations, mechanism-isolation experiments, parameter sensitivity analysis, and broadband simulations under realistic offshore sea-state excitation. The simulation results indicate that, whilst the hydraulic response is governed primarily by wave propagation phenomena, compressibility, and boundary reflections, the structural dynamics display substantially greater sensitivity to distributed friction effects. Furthermore, drillstring-wellbore friction is shown to have a relatively limited influence on well-posedness but a potentially significant impact on stability margins. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for coupled hydraulic-structural dynamics and distributed friction mechanisms when analysing, monitoring, and controlling offshore drilling systems.

papers.title: Composition loci, invariant Bezoutians, and finite-orbit correspondences
papers.abstract: We compute projective degrees of composition loci for polynomial and rational maps of the projective line. For normalized polynomials of degree $rs$ with a right composition factor of degree $s$, a projective-bundle construction gives the degree $S(r+s-2,r)$. We extend this calculation to composition chains, and obtain $S(r+s-1,r)$ in the uncentered normalization used for decomposable interpolation. For rational maps, a Grassmann-bundle model gives a Pl\"ucker degree formula and an interpretation by prescribed critical points. We relate these loci to factorization of the Bezoutian in the ring of symmetric polynomials, where factors correspond to monodromy orbits on unordered pairs. Fried's polynomial criterion then determines the invariant reducibility locus. For rational maps we determine its composition components when a marked pole fiber has exactly one ramified point and at least one unramified point. The qualitative equivalence between finite full orbits and a first integral is already known. We give a direct proof from forward stabilization, with an explicit test using bounded forward orbits and with quotient fibers identified at every point. We also determine when absolute and invariant irreducibility differ and give a growth formula for a class of translation correspondences.

papers.title: Intrinsic reduction data and the loci related to indeterminacy of iterate maps for rational functions
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of not necessarily characteristic $0$, and $d,n$ be integers $\ge 2$. We first formulate the dynamical moduli spaces of rational functions defined over $k$ in terms of the intrinsic reduction data of non-archimedean rational functions. As an application, we show that the locus $C_{d,n}$ of semistable intrinsic reduction data in degree $d$ whose $n$th iteration is defined and unstable is of codimension $d$ in the intrinsic reduction data space of degree $d$, settling a conjecture of Kiwi and Nie, and show that the image of $C_{d,n}$ in the compactified dynamical moduli $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{d,k}$ is of dimension $\le d-2$ and the equality holds precisely either if $d$ is even or if $d\ge 5$ is odd and $(4/d)^n<1/(d-3)$ and determine the dimensions even for all the five exceptional pairs $(d,n)$, in addition describing the images of $C_{3,n}$ themselves. We also determine the indeterminacy of iterate maps either on the intrinsic reduction data spaces or on the compactified dynamical moduli spaces.

papers.title: A Dynamical N\'eron--Ogg--Shafarevich Criterion via Orbital Arboreal Representations
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a non-archimedean local field and $\varphi : \mathbb{P}^1 \to \mathbb{P}^1$ a rational endomorphism of degree $d \geq 2$ over $K$. In the tame case ($p \nmid d$), we show that strict good reduction is equivalent to the existence of a nonempty Zariski open subset $U_k \subset \mathbb{P}^1_k \setminus \mathrm{PC}(\widetilde{\varphi})$ over which the canonical residual morphism is finite \'etale of degree $d$. The criterion separates two complementary local invariants of a normalized integral lift: $\mathrm{Res}(F,G)$ controls residual degree drop, while the fiber discriminants $\mathrm{Disc}(F_{n,x})$ control \'etaleness of the residual fibers once full residual degree is ensured. Consequently, for every finite $x \in \mathcal{O}_K$ with $\bar{x} \in U_k$, the extensions $K(X_n(x))/K$ are unramified for all $n \geq 1$. We introduce the orbital preimage tree $T_{O^+(x)} = \varinjlim_n X_\infty(\varphi^n(x))$, the colimit in $G_K$-sets along the forward orbit, and the orbital arboreal Galois image $\mathcal{G}_{O^+(x)} = \mathrm{Im}(G_K \to \mathrm{Aut}(T_{O^+(x)}))$. On the forward-invariant safe locus $U_k^{\mathrm{safe}} = \bigcap_{m \geq 0} \widetilde{\varphi}^{-m}(U_k)$, strict good reduction is captured by the bijectivity of the orbital reduction map $X_n(x_m) \to \widetilde{X}_n(\bar{x}_m)$. This canonical orbit-invariant framework connects with arboreal Galois representations (Boston-Jones, Jones, and others) and yields pointwise and orbit-level reformulations. Explicit examples over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ illustrate the criterion.

papers.title: Stability of equilibria in discrete-time modified-gradient systems and the multivariate breeder's equation
papers.abstract:
The multivariate breeder's equation $\Delta ar z=G
abla\ln ar W$ is a widely used discrete-time modified-gradient system describing the evolution of continuous traits in organisms. This system could more conventionally be expressed as $x_{k+1}=x_k+P_k
abla f(x_k)$. For its continuous-time counterpart $x'=P(t)
abla f(x)$, it has been proven that an isolated local maximum of $f$ is uniformly stable whenever $P(t)$ is positive semidefinite, as is the case for the "$G$-matrix." Furthermore, the continuous time system is uniformly asymptotically stable when the maximum is an isolated critical point and $\int_0^\infty\lambda_1(P(t))\,dt=\infty$. We show that the literal discrete analog of this result is false: with constant positive definite $P$ the iterates can oscillate or diverge. The result is restored by a single additional hypothesis, a uniform bound on the largest eigenvalue of $P_k$, $\lambda_n$, such that $\lambda_n(P_k)\le 2/L$ where $L$ is a local Lipschitz constant of $
abla f$. Under this bound the maximum is uniformly stable; under a stricter version together with $\sum_k\lambda_1(P_k)=\infty$, the maximum is uniformly asymptotically stable. Given these hypotheses, a level-set estimate of the basin of attraction carries over. Both bounds are sharp, and each remaining hypothesis is shown to be necessary. Biologically, the bound says that genetic variance in every direction must be small relative to the curvature of log mean fitness; outside this regime the mean phenotype can overshoot a fitness peak as hypothesized by Fisher's geometric model. As further application of our results, the same conditions apply to the mean update of Gaussian evolutionary optimization algorithms, in which the covariance of the search population plays the role of $G$.

papers.title: Sharpness of the acceleration-dependent H\"older exponent for the integrated density of states
papers.abstract: We prove that the acceleration-dependent H\"older exponent $1/(2\omega)$ for the integrated density of states is sharp in the supercritical regime. For every positive integer $k$ and every Diophantine frequency, we construct a real even trigonometric polynomial potential of degree $k$ such that, at a spectral edge, the Lyapunov exponent is positive, the acceleration is $k$, and the exact local H\"older exponent is $1/(2k)$. In particular, the $1/2$-H\"older regularity of the subcritical regime for Diophantine frequencies does not hold in general in the supercritical regime. The proof uses Aubry duality and a KAM iteration that adjusts the potential coefficients to make the dual cocycle reducible to a principal unipotent matrix. A comparison with an explicit reference family and symplectic block diagonalization then reduce the IDS estimate to a two-dimensional rotation-number estimate.

papers.title: Canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction
papers.abstract: We study canard explosions in mass-action networks with one slow direction. For any number of species and any rank of the fast subnetwork, the derivatives that enter the Krupa-Szmolyan conditions and coefficient are rational functions of the fluxes and the reciprocal concentrations. For a fast subnetwork of rank one, the dynamics is planar on stoichiometric classes and these forms are linear in the fluxes, extending our planar flux criterion; the criticality is an explicit cubic. When one species is fast, these forms decompose over the slow species, weighted by their reciprocal concentrations. The elementary-mode criterion then carries over, and the criticality depends on the composition of the slow pool, so one network can explode in either way. The obstruction that the slow flux cannot vanish on the fold is characterised by a Farkas certificate and a yield diagram decided on configurations of at most three reactions. Under four conditions on the critical curve, a canard point with $A\neq0$ unfolded by a rate constant gives the full canard explosion; with one fast species and a fast equation affine in the slow variable, these follow from sign conditions on the reactions and injectivity on the class. For fast subnetworks of higher rank, a centre-manifold reduction adds corrections through the group inverse of the fast Jacobian; in the Oregonator they make both canard points change criticality between its planar reduction and the full model. All results are proved; exact computations and simulations serve as independent checks.

papers.title: Rigidity of time changes of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flows on finite volume quotients
papers.abstract: We study the rigidity phenomenon of the time changed unipotent flows on general Lie groups. Under some spectral gap assumptions, we prove that every ergodic nonsplitting $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow on a finite volume quotient space $\mathbf{G}/\Gamma$ is time changed rigid. We also prove that for $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-induced unipotent flow, the splitting condition is equivalent to loosely Kroneckerness. Our result in particular applies to $\mathbf{G}=\mathbf{S}\ltimes\mathbf{N}$, where $\mathbf{S}$ is the identity component of a real semisimple linear algebraic group without compact factors and $\mathbf{N}$ is simply connected and connected nilpotent Lie group. These are extensions of [KVW21,LW25].

papers.title: Zero-Hopf Networks
papers.abstract: A zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur for dynamical systems that have a singularity where the linear part has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. We call a zero-Hopf network a regular network whose adjacency matrix has a zero eigenvalue and a pair of complex eigenvalues with zero real part. In this work, we prove that there is an infinite number of zero-Hopf networks for which the zero-Hopf bifurcation can occur as a generic codimension-one phenomenon for the class of the network admissible smooth vector fields. Our results are achieved using the network adjacency matrices and the associated eigenvector structures. General results are presented for four-cell zero-Hopf networks concerning the network set of synchrony spaces. As a case study, we present a classification of all connected zero-Hopf 4-cell regular networks of valency two showing that, up to permutation of the cells, there are 9 distinct such networks. Moreover, the normal forms of these networks are computed using the method of Rink and Sanders (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 367 (2015) 3509--3548) for coupled cell networks. It is remarked that these normal forms are less simplified as the input symmetry of the network admissible smooth vector fields restricts the admissible normal form transformations. Nevertheless, the networks share a common coupling function normal form.

papers.title: Stability of analytic monodromic singularities without curves of zero angular speed
papers.abstract: The aim of this work is to give conditions on the parameters of a family of analytic planar vector fields with a fixed Newton diagram and a monodromic singularity in order to guarantee that the coefficient (generalized first Lyapunov constant) of the linear part of the Poincar\'e map has an explicit formula. We revisit using this formalism some monodromic examples appearing in the literature and also we apply the results to other families were, as far as we know, the stability problem was open.

papers.title: Universal Realization of Milnor Attractors in Low Dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the realization problem for Milnor attractors on compact metric spaces and establish a general sufficient criterion for universal realization. In particular, we prove that every smooth compact one-dimensional manifold, with or without boundary, and every smooth closed two-dimensional manifold has the property that each nonempty closed subset is the Milnor global attractor of a continuous self-map. If the manifold is connected, the realizing map may be chosen to be a homeomorphism. We also investigate the realization problem on selected one-dimensional continua and exhibit spaces for which universal realization fails.

papers.title: On the structure of the sets of connections between libration points and some applications
papers.abstract: This paper presents a methodology for the global description of the sets of heteroclinic and homoclinic connections between the center manifolds of the collinear libration points of the spatial circular Restricted Three-Body Problem. The approach builds on high-order parameterizations of the center-stable and center-unstable invariant manifolds and uses them to extract global information on how connections are organized across broad energy ranges. It involves: (a) constructing connectivity maps at the level of invariant tori, which encode which tori in the neighborhoods of $L_1$ and $L_2$ are connected through heteroclinic and homoclinic trajectories; (b) refining this description to the level of individual connections by computing traces of torus--center manifold connections and using them to determine the number and distribution of distinct connecting trajectories between selected pairs of tori. Results are given for the Earth--Moon and Sun--Earth problems, together with examples illustrating how the resulting connectivity information can be used to design heteroclinic and homoclinic pseudo-trajectories with different purposes.

papers.title: Geometric structure of Green currents for holomorphic correspondences on projective surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic correspondence on a complex projective surface $X$ such that $f^{-1}$ is also holomorphic. Assume that the action of $f^*$ on cohomology is simple and that the dynamical degrees of $f$ satisfy $d_1>\max\{d_0,d_2\}$. We prove that the Green currents $T^\pm$ associated with $f$ are woven. We also provide a large family of examples of holomorphic correspondences satisfying our assumptions, obtained as generic complete intersections in $X\times X$.

papers.title: Equidistribution of Hecke neighbours and continued fraction patterns
papers.abstract: We prove uniform tightness of Hecke neighbours of any probability measure of positive entropy that is invariant and ergodic under the diagonal flow. As an application, we confirm a conjecture of Einsiedler concerning a homogeneous dynamics analogue of an equidistribution theorem of Johnson and Rudolph on the torus. We also obtain applications to continued-fraction patterns in arithmetic sequences and to the \(p\)-adic Littlewood conjecture. Our proof studies escape of mass using dynamics on the boundary of the Chabauty compactification of the space of lattices, together with averaging operators defined by leafwise measures along horospherical subgroups.

papers.title: Autonomous Neural Adaptive Control as a Self-Consistent Transfer Operator
papers.abstract: We study autonomous neural adaptive control, where the controller modifies the physical dynamics while the data generated by the physical dynamics itself drive subsequent parameter updates. We formulate the coupled evolution of the physical state distribution and controller parameters through a self-consistent transfer operator. Assuming that the physical dynamics under each fixed controller admits a unique invariant distribution, we characterize adaptive equilibria through a finite-dimensional self-consistency equation for the stationary mean learning update. We establish existence using Brouwer degree, without requiring global convexity, and reduce uniqueness to uniqueness of the corresponding zero. Under suitable differentiability and spectral-gap assumptions, we derive a finite-dimensional criterion for local exponential convergence of both the physical distribution and controller parameters at sufficiently small positive learning rates. The criterion involves the Jacobian of the reduced equation, computed using linear response to include the effect of controller-induced changes in the invariant distribution. The asymptotic slow relaxation time scales inversely with the learning rate. We rigorously verify the assumptions and apply the theory to a noisy Duffing-type system with a neural residual compensator, providing a nontrivial example of adaptive control with provable existence, uniqueness, and local stability of an adaptive equilibrium. Numerical experiments illustrate statistical feedback and the role of time-scale separation.

papers.title: Density of periodic measures on $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb R)$ with prescribed arithmetic information
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be the diagonal flow on the modular space $X_2$, and let $\mathcal{S}_f$ be the set of positive square-free numbers, which is identified with the set of all real quadratic fields via the natural map $d\mapsto \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt d)$. In this paper, we prove that, for any finite subset $A\subseteq\mathcal{S}_f$, there exists a density-zero set $B\subseteq\mathcal{S}_f\setminus A$ such that the set of all $F$-periodic measures with associated quadratic fields from $B$ is dense in the set of all $F$-invariant measures on $X_2$.

papers.title: Shift-Symmetric Configurations in $d$-Dimensional Cellular Automata: Enumeration, Bounds, Irreversibility, and Detection
papers.abstract: A configuration of a cellular automaton on the $d$-dimensional torus $\mathbb{Z}_n^d$ is shift-symmetric if it is fixed by some nonzero translation. Banda, Caughman, Cenek, and Teuscher (Chaos 29, 063120, 2019) enumerated these configurations in two dimensions and drew dynamical and algorithmic consequences. We extend their results to every dimension. We give an explicit closed-form enumeration for all $n$, $d$, and alphabet sizes $\sigma$, in which the two-dimensional coefficients $1$, $p+1$, and $p$ become $r_d(p,v)=p^{\binom{v}{2}}\binom{d}{v}_p$, with $\binom{d}{v}_p$ the Gaussian binomial; it extends to configurations with a prescribed number of active cells and to all finite abelian groups. The case of prime $n$ recovers, in complement form, a result of Castillo-Ramirez and Gadouleau; the multi-prime closed form and the dynamical consequences beyond the stabilizer inclusion are new. We prove a lower bound attained exactly when $n$ is prime, and upper bounds, among them $(2^d-1+2\log_2 n)\,\sigma^{n^d/2}$. As $d$ grows, the symmetry probability decays as $\sigma^{-c\,n^d}$ with $c\to1-1/p_1(n)$, set solely by the smallest prime factor of $n$, and the symmetry advantage of the side $p+1$ over a prime side $p$ inverts within an explicit window around $d_c(p)\approx p\ln 2$. Under the necessary hypothesis of translation-equivariant neighborhoods, shift-symmetry is irreversible, the per-prime symmetry ranks never decrease, and non-symmetric tasks are unsolvable from symmetric inputs. We give a detection algorithm with worst-case cost $O(n^d\sum_{p\mid n}\frac{p^d-1}{p-1})$ and an average-case analysis, exact for each subgroup test. The mathematical content of every numbered statement is formally verified in Lean 4, and the correspondence between each theorem, lemma, proposition, and corollary and its formal statement was audited by hand.

papers.title: Almost sure behaviour of empirical measures for intermittent maps whose return time distribution is 1-regularly varying
papers.abstract: In this article we study sets of limit points $\mathcal{L}$ for the sequence of empirical measures of intermittent maps with several equally sticky neutral fixed points. Such intermittent maps come with a parameter $\alpha > 0$ which determines the "stickiness" of the neutral fixed points. When $\alpha \neq 1$, it is known that two different behaviours can occur: either $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely the singleton $\{\mu\}$ where $\mu$ is an absolutely continuous invariant probability measure; or $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely given by the entire simplex $\pi\mathcal{S}$ of invariant measures supported at the neutral fixed points. We study the case that $\alpha = 1$ and show that neither of these two behaviours occur and that $\mathcal{L}$ is almost surely equal to a star-shaped subset of the simplex $\pi \mathcal{S}$. Moreover, we show that when slowly varying functions are introduced one can obtain a large range of different behaviours, including both the possible outcomes when $\alpha \neq 1$. Our results apply to a large class of intermittent interval maps as well as parabolic rational maps of the Riemann sphere.

papers.title: The Levitt--Yoccoz gasket: dynamics, Hausdorff dimension and norm exponent
papers.abstract: In S.P.~Novikov's problem on plane sections of 3ply periodic surfaces, the author and I.\,A.~Dynnikov showed that, for the $\mu$-cube, the directions lying in no stability zone form the union of a fractal set $N$, the Levitt--Yoccoz gasket (projectively equivalent to the Rauzy gasket), and of its images under the sign changes of the coordinates. $N$ is the limit set of a parabolic projective iterated function system $P\Gamma_N$ generated by a semigroup $\Gamma_N\subset SL_3(\mathbb Z)$, and each zone is labelled by a primitive integer vector, its soul. We show that $N$ is the global attractor of $P\Gamma_N$ and that the chain graphs of $P\Gamma_N$ and its Hutchinson map consist of a single node. Building on the theorem of Jiao--Li--Pan--Xu and Jurga that $\dim_H N$ equals the affinity exponent of $\Gamma_N$, we prove $1.6853<\dim_HN=\dim_BN<1.6854$. For some class of cut-out gaskets $K$, we bound $\overline{\dim}_B K$ from both sides by the norm exponent $s_N(\Gamma)$. The norm exponent $s_N$ of $G_N$, the counting exponent of the souls, is Baragar's exponent of the Markoff--Hurwitz equation $x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2+x_4^2=ax_1x_2x_3x_4$. We prove $2.4411\le s_N\le2.4465$, improving Baragar's bounds, and $\frac23 s_N\le\dim_H N\le\frac12(1+s_N)$, which proves a conjecture by Gamburd, Magee and Ronan; and we show that the exponent of the equation in six variables exceeds $3$, answering a question of Baragar. For the three-dimensional Levitt--Yoccoz gasket $G\subset\mathbb RP^3$ we prove $2.74\le s_N(\Gamma_G)\le2.777$ and $\dim_H G\le2.3885$. Finally, for the renormalization flow of Avila, Hubert and Skripchenko, we show that the invariant measure they introduce is the Gibbs measure at the parameter $s_N$ and that $s_N$ is the maximal entropy per unit time of the return map, attained only by this measure. So, the diffusion exponent of their chaotic plane sections is less than 0.7766.

papers.title: Invariant random compacts for $\times p, \times q$ on the circle
papers.abstract: We prove that for multiplicatively independent natural numbers $p,q \ge 2$, if $\mu$ is a Borel probability measure on the space $\mathcal{K}(\mathbb{T})$ of nonempty compact subsets of the circle $\mathbb{T}$ which is invariant under the induced actions of both multiplication by $p$ and $q$, and $\mu$-a.e. $Y$ has positive Hausdorff dimension, then $\mu$-a.e. $Y$ is equal to $\mathbb{T}$.

papers.title: Nondifferentiability on Irrational Invariant Graphs of Smooth Area-Preserving Twist Maps
papers.abstract: For a fixed irrational rotation number and every $1\le r<\infty$, we construct an exact area-preserving $C^r$ twist map preserving a Lipschitz graph. The set of nondifferentiability points has Hausdorff dimension $d=2/(r+1)$ and zero $d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. At the same rotation number, we construct a $C^\infty$ twist map whose invariant graph is nondifferentiable on exactly one two-sided orbit. The dynamics on these graphs has wandering intervals.

papers.title: Weighted summability criteria for stability and instability of discrete dynamics with general growth rates
papers.abstract: Following the time rescaling introduced by Dragi\v{c}evi\'{c} and Silva in their paper [Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst. Ser. S 18 (2025), 3917--3944], we establish several criteria for uniform $h$-stability and uniform $h$-instability of discrete evolution cocycles. In particular, these asymptotic properties are characterized by suitable weighted summability conditions under uniform $h$-boundedness and uniform $h$-decay assumptions, respectively. Explicit examples show that the respective assumptions cannot be omitted. Our results cover a wide range of discrete growth rates $h$, including exponential and polynomial ones. Furthermore, working in the general setting of discrete evolution cocycles, we provide a framework for discrete evolution families and discrete cocycles.

papers.title: Quantitative flocking of Cucker-Smale flocks under time-delay and noise
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic flocking dynamics of the delayed stochastic Cucker-Smale (in short, DSCS) model driven by agent-wise independent, component-wise multiplicative Brownian noise. The simultaneous interplay of stochastic perturbations and time delay yields fundamental challenges to asymptotic stochastic flocking analysis, as the communication weight may lose a uniform positive lower bound, while the velocity moment is no longer monotone. To overcome these difficulties, we present a sufficient framework and an analytical tool combining the method of time-varying effective region and Lyapunov functional approach with time-delay corrections. This approach avoids any reliance on uniformly positive communication weights or monotone velocity moments. The proposed approach recovers sufficiently strong effective velocity alignment despite stochastic fluctuations and delay effects. As a consequence, we establish the mean-square stochastic flocking with an explicit polynomial convergence rate. The admissible decay exponent is determined by the communication kernel exponent and the orders of the spatial and velocity history moments. These results establish a quantitative theory for long-time stochastic flocking under simultaneous delay and multiplicative noise, and we provide a positive answer to an open problem raised by~[R. Erban, J. Haskovec, Y. Sun, SIAM J. Appl. Math., 76, 1535--1557 (2016)]. We also develop robust analytical tools applicable to delayed stochastic collective dynamics with degenerate communications.

papers.title: Quantitative Accumulation of Invariant Circles Near a Non-splitting Separatrix
papers.abstract: For a smooth area-preserving cylinder map with a non-splitting separatrix and an exact symplectic linearization at its saddle, we prove accumulation by smooth essential invariant circles when the boundary transition is sufficiently $C^4$-close to a translation. As an application, we give an answer to Herman's open problem in 1983.

papers.title: Infectious Disease Horizon in Emerging Infectious Diseases
papers.abstract: Emerging infectious diseases often spread freely before an outbreak is detected, yet the duration of this free-transmission period and the infection size accumulated during this period are difficult to quantify. These quantities directly affect forecasts of subsequent transmission dynamics, estimates of infection size, and decisions regarding prevention and control measures. In this study, we propose and compute the infectious disease horizon (IDH)-the time span from when an infectious disease begins spreading to when it is first detected-and examine its antecedents and consequences. First, based on the SEAIR free-transmission model, we derive transmission characteristics, including the generation interval, the serial interval, the basic reproduction number, and the effective reproduction number, and describe the incidence using a renewal equation. Second, by considering two detection routes, we further obtain the distribution and mean of the IDH under different detection settings and quantify the infection size at the time of outbreak detection. Third, intervention measures are incorporated to derive a post-detection transmission model with generally distributed stage durations, followed by the derivation of the corresponding model under exponentially distributed stage durations and the determination of the final infection size. Finally, under the exponential-distribution assumption, the model is applied to the COVID-19 outbreak in Xi'an. The unified framework developed in this study provides a theoretical basis for evaluating early surveillance capacity for emerging infectious diseases, optimizing testing strategies, and determining the intensity of prevention and control measures after outbreak detection.

papers.title: Data-Driven Discovery and Rigorous Certification of Periodic Solutions in Infinite-Dimensional Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: In this work, we consider a standard regression technique for time series analysis which fits a low-dimensional proxy system to a higher (even infinite) dimensional target model. We then propose a novel diagnostic that exploits a-posteriori computer-assisted proofs, and try to certify the existence of a true periodic solution of the target, nearby. When successful, this certification procedure provides mathematically rigorous information about how well an invariant structure in the proxy approximates a corresponding invariant structure in the target model. To illustrate the utility of the procedure, we develop surrogates using time series data from the Mackey--Glass delay differential equation, and for the Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) partial differential equation, using periodic boundary conditions for forecasting and Neumann boundary conditions for certification. In both test cases we extract invariant dynamics from low-dimensional proxies and use this to validate the existence of corresponding structures in the targets.
